correctness.rationale: A newly formed 132 pattern during an adjacent swap must use the swapped pair, yielding necessary/sufficient local criterion: ascent x<y may swap when no earlier z<x; descent x>y may swap when no later y<z<x. Repeatedly swapping leftmost ascent reaches the reverse permutation and proves connectivity. To move n left past each b<n legally, every pair a<b<n must reverse orientation twice, giving 2*binom(n-1,2)+(n-1)=(n-1)^2; a constructed ascent-sort-to-reverse followed by legal suffix sorting achieves exactly this. Catalan maximum decomposition yields E(z)=z(C(z)-1)/(1-2zC(z)), whose n coefficient is binom(2n-2,n-2). Independently constructed all 132 avoiders and full swap graph for 2<=n<=8, checked exact vertices, edges, connectivity and BFS distance, without extrapolating finite tests to all n.

value.rationale: The exact ratio n-1 between intrinsic and ambient geodesic distances is unbounded in an induced Catalan permutohedron subgraph. It is a concrete structural obstruction to assuming pattern-avoiding induced paths preserve the ambient metric and comes with the natural full vertex/edge count; it is neither an arbitrary small-case statistic nor an unsupported diameter assertion.

final_claim: For all n>=2 the adjacent-swap induced graph on classical 132-avoiding permutations is connected, has Catalan C_n vertices and binom(2n-2,n-2) edges, and its exact distance between identity e_n and one-step right rotation (n,1,...,n-1) is (n-1)^2 versus unrestricted adjacent-swap distance n-1; no diameter theorem.
limitations: Classical 132-pattern avoidance, standard adjacent-position swaps only; exact distance for one canonical endpoint pair, not graph diameter.
